finding.claim: When the application passes subject=, _validate_sub returns early if the token has no sub claim, so a validly signed token without sub passes a subject-bound check. Plausible, medium-low; depends on the app using subject= and the issuer also minting tokens without sub.
finding.source: Attacker holds any token validly signed by the same issuer/key that lacks a sub claim (e.g. service or anonymous token).
finding.sink: Application subject-bound authorization after jwt.decode(..., subject=...) succeeds.

finding.guards_checked: Signature verified before claims (api_jws.py:416) so token must come from issuer; exp/aud/iss still enforced; _validate_iss (api_jwt.py:571-572) and _validate_aud (529-532) fail closed on missing claim, showing inconsistency; options require=['sub'] would mitigate but is not default.

finding.claim: base64url_decode uses non-strict base64 decoding, so the signature segment accepts non-canonical encodings (junk non-alphabet chars, unused trailing bits, high-S ECDSA). Different token strings verify for the same token. Plausible, low; impact depends on app keying replay/revocation on the raw token string.
finding.source: Attacker holds one valid token and mutates the signature segment.
finding.sink: Application replay/denylist or one-time-use check keyed on the raw token string.
